newsitem.title: GREECE: Hard drachma helps push WPI inflation down in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Hard drachma helps push WPI inflation down in Jan.

text.p: The Bank of Greece's hard drachma policy helped push prices of imported final goods lower by 1.3 percent year-on-year in January and WPI (wholesale price index) inflation to 3.1 percent year-on-year in the same month, National Statistics Service (NSS) figures showed.
WPI-based inflation stood at 3.9 percent year-on-year in December when the sub-WPI index of imported final goods had posted another drop of 0.90 percent year-on-year.
The hard drahma policy aims to keep the drachma broadly stable against the currencies that make up the ecu in 1997. It is the main anti-inflationary policy tool of the central bank.

The Bank of Greece has said that it wants CPI (consumer price index) inflation to be at 4.5 percent at end-1997 and below 3.0 percent at end-98. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
